blocks.text: Hi Elizabeth,
One item to add to Jeffrey's note. It concerns the plan document, not the census, but we need both before we calculate any benefit.

A valuation measures the benefits the plan actually promises as of the valuation date. That means the provisions as amended, not as originally written. A provision we have to infer becomes an assumption, and we avoid making one where a document exists.

Please send the current plan document for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}, with each amendment adopted since it was last restated. If there have been no amendments, a one-line reply saying so is enough. The secure file site is the best route for the document itself.

Once it is in hand, David will code the provisions into the model alongside the census. We will then send you a short summary of the data and provisions as we have them, kept separate from any assumption.

Sincerely,
Jennifer

blocks.text: Working Session Minutes: Pension Valuation for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}

The census is now final for valuation purposes, subject to one open item, and the assumption review has a clear path forward. We closed the terminated vested questions, confirmed the plan provisions, and walked through a first look at the plan's experience. No assumption was adopted at this session, and nothing recorded below should be read as a recommendation.
Present

items: Elizabeth Horne, Director of Operations, {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}}
Jennifer Vasquez, Consulting Actuary
David Sherman, Senior Analyst
Jeffrey Ochoa, Actuarial Analyst (minutes)

blocks.text: Census reconciliation

David Sherman opened with the reconciliation. The active and retiree records had tied to the prior year's file on the first pass, so the discussion centered on the terminated vested records that showed no supporting change of status. Elizabeth Horne had traced most of them to former employees who took lump-sum payments and were never removed from the file. We agreed those records come out of the valuation, and David will document the source of each removal in the data summary.

A small number of active records still lack a date of hire, and Elizabeth expects payroll can supply them. Jennifer Vasquez drew a line between this and the earlier problem. An unexplained status change leaves us unsure whether the person belongs in the valuation at all, while a missing hire date leaves one data element open for someone who plainly does. If the dates do not arrive in time, David will carry those participants on a stated assumption and flag it in the summary so the gap stays visible.
Plan provisions

The restated plan document and its amendments arrived after our last exchange. Jennifer has reviewed them against the coding in the model, and the benefit calculations now reflect the provisions as amended. She asked that we hear about any amendment under consideration, since a change adopted before the report is issued may need to be reflected or disclosed.
Experience and assumptions

Jeffrey Ochoa presented the first look at retirement and termination experience. What the data show is that participants have been retiring later than the current retirement rates assume, most clearly at the first age at which an unreduced benefit is available. That is an observation drawn from a short period of experience, and we kept it apart from any recommendation. Recommended rates will come with the full study, together with a view on how much weight the plan's own experience can carry.

On mortality, Jennifer explained that the current basis predates the RP-2014 table and the MP-2015 improvement scale the Society of Actuaries published last fall. Moving to the newer basis is a judgment, and for most plans it has meant longer assumed lifetimes and higher liabilities. Elizabeth asked how large the effect would be here. Jennifer declined to give a figure before the data are final and the other assumptions are set, because an estimate offered now tends to be quoted later as a result. We agreed instead to show the effect of the mortality change on its own line in the preliminary results.
Agreed actions

Once the hire dates are in, or on a stated assumption if they are not

Status Report: Pension Valuation
Prepared for {{fact:f:E-2016-001.client}} by Meridian Actuarial Advisors. This report covers the work through the midpoint of the engagement. It contains no valuation results.
Position at the Midpoint
The valuation is on schedule and within the scope set out in the engagement letter. The census data are final, the plan provisions are confirmed, and the assumption review is under way.
No results have been produced, and none will be until the assumptions are agreed. One decision is needed from you before then, on the mortality basis. It is set out at the end of this report.
Completed to Date

items: Received the participant census and loaded it into the valuation model.
Reconciled the census to the prior year's file. Active and retiree records tied on the first pass.

Resolved the terminated vested records with your staff at the working session. Former employees who had been paid lump sums but remained on the file were removed, and the source of each removal is documented.
Obtained the missing hire dates from payroll, which closed the last open data item.
Received the restated plan document and its amendments, and reflected the amended provisions in the benefit calculations.
Issued the written data summary, prepared by David Sherman, listing each change made to the file and its source.
Completed a first review of retirement and termination experience, prepared by Jeffrey Ochoa.

blocks.text: What the Data Show

The census, as reconciled, is complete and internally consistent for every participant group. Each record now carries the elements the valuation needs, and no participant is carried on an assumed data value.

The experience review shows participants retiring later than the current rates assume. The pattern is clearest at the first age at which an unreduced benefit is available. It rests on a short period of data and is an observation, not yet a recommendation.
What Has Been Assumed
No new assumptions have been adopted. To test the data and provisions end to end, the model is running on the prior valuation's assumptions as a placeholder.
Output on that basis is a check on the mechanics only. It is not reported and should not be relied on for any purpose.

The economic assumptions will be proposed together with the demographic set, each with its basis stated in writing. Any item set by regulation will be identified as prescribed rather than presented as our selection.
What We Conclude at This Stage
The data are adequate for the valuation. That conclusion is limited to their consistency and completeness, which is the review called for under Actuarial Standard of Practice No. 23, Data Quality.
We have relied on the census and plan documents as provided and have not audited them. We reach no conclusion yet on the plan's liabilities or costs.
Work Ahead

rows: Recommended retirement and termination rates, with the supporting study
Mortality comparison: current basis against RP-2014 with MP-2015
Assumption review meeting with your staff
Preliminary valuation results, with the mortality effect shown separately
Your review of the preliminary results

blocks.text: Risks to the Schedule

items: Assumption decisions. Preliminary results cannot be run until the assumptions are agreed, and each later step moves with that decision.
Plan changes. An amendment adopted before the report is issued may need to be reflected or disclosed. Please tell us of any change under consideration.
Experience period. The period studied is short. If the retirement pattern weakens in the full study, we will recommend a partial move toward it and state why.
Data corrections. A census correction from this point requires the reconciliation to be re-run for the records it affects. We will tell you before any re-run changes the schedule.

blocks.text: Decision Needed: Mortality Basis

The mortality basis is the largest open judgment in this valuation. The current basis predates the RP-2014 table and the MP-2015 improvement scale, and for most plans the newer basis has meant longer assumed lifetimes and higher liabilities.

We will show the effect of the change on its own line in the preliminary results, so it can be seen apart from every other assumption. We ask that you be prepared to decide on the basis at the assumption review meeting, after you have seen that effect.
Questions on this report may go to Jennifer Vasquez. David Sherman can answer questions on the data summary, and Jeffrey Ochoa on the experience review.
